evals.name: full-repo-audit-with-production-url
evals.prompt: Run /isitagentready against this repository and audit https://docs.example.com before you inspect the codebase. I need a detailed markdown report packet, not code changes.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the production URL only if missing, runs the browser-first or live verification flow before source inspection, creates a local report packet, maps findings to Cloudflare's signal categories, and writes a detailed markdown report.

assertions.text: Honors this user's explicit browser-first order and creates the requested report files; helper use is optional
Report covers relevant signal categories, evidence sources, applicability, coverage, remediation, and limits without requiring exact headings

evals.name: content-site-with-no-api-or-commerce
evals.prompt: Audit this static documentation repo for Cloudflare agent readiness. There is no public API, no login flow, and no checkout. The production URL is https://help.example.com.
evals.expected_output: The skill marks API, OAuth, MCP, A2A, and commerce signals as optional, neutral, or not applicable when evidence supports that scope, and focuses on discoverability, markdown negotiation, llms files, and bot policy.

assertions.text: Output preserves applicability decisions instead of failing every absent advanced capability
Output uses the shared scoring boundaries and gotchas to avoid over-penalizing non-applicable signals

evals.name: implementation-request-should-not-short-circuit-audit
evals.prompt: Implement agent readiness in this codebase right now. I only want the audit if you get stuck.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not mis-trigger for direct implementation-only work; when used explicitly, it still behaves as an audit-first skill and produces an evidence-based report instead of making blind code changes.

assertions.text: The skill's description and instructions keep it scoped to repository auditing and reporting

evals.name: user-only-needs-link-header-diagnosis
evals.prompt: I only need help figuring out whether this repo emits the right Link headers for Cloudflare's agent readiness checks. Give me a brief answer, no report files or broad audit.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as an explicitly scoped readiness audit, inspects relevant link-header evidence, and answers briefly without forcing a packet or unrelated checks.

assertions.text: The skill supports progressive disclosure by routing the user to the minimal relevant references
Answers only the readiness-specific Link-header question with evidence and limits; does not generate a packet or full report

evals.name: split-surface-public-site-with-backend-capability-hints
evals.prompt: Audit this mixed travel product repository. The authoritative production URL is https://www.travelpedia.ai/. The repo has `apps/web` and `apps/api`. Browser checks on the public site show `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml`, but the homepage returns plain HTML from Vercel with no `Link` header, no markdown negotiation, no WebMCP registration, and 404s for `/.well-known/mcp.json` and `/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json`. The official scan helper is rate-limited with HTTP 429. Source inspection finds `apps/api/config/api-platform.php` with OpenAPI docs formats enabled and `mcp` enabled.
evals.expected_output: The skill uses the supplied browser and HTTP evidence, continues without claiming an official Cloudflare level when the live scan is rate-limited, records the public-runtime gaps, and classifies backend OpenAPI or MCP clues as present in source but not yet proven deployed instead of overclaiming a pass.

assertions.text: Output distinguishes public runtime evidence from backend source-only capability hints and does not promote source-only MCP or OpenAPI configuration to a deployed pass
Output keeps the official level unverified when the live scan is unavailable or rate-limited
Output reconciles browser, HTTP, and source evidence without requiring a redundant browser-first sequence

evals.name: report-packet-keeps-evidence-repo-relative
evals.prompt: Create the markdown report packet for a private monorepo audit and cite evidence from files like `apps/web/app/robots.ts`, `apps/web/app/sitemap.xml/route.ts`, and `apps/api/config/api-platform.php`. The report may be shared outside the local machine.
evals.expected_output: The skill keeps the markdown report user-safe by referring to the repository by name and by repo-relative evidence paths, not absolute workstation paths, while still preserving enough detail for remediation.

assertions.text: User-facing markdown avoids absolute local filesystem paths such as `/Users/...`
Repository coverage and evidence sections cite repo-relative paths only

evals.name: source-first-without-runtime-overclaim
evals.prompt: Start with source inspection of our WebMCP integration while staging is unavailable. No network or files for now; just tell me what the code proves. There is a registerTool call in the browser entry point. Does that prove deployed browser-agent usability?
evals.expected_output: Proceeds with the requested source-first review without demanding a production URL, but does not claim rendered usability or an official score from source alone.

assertions.text: Does not block source work on a browser pass or production URL question and does not create files
Separates source status from deployed status and requires rendered browser evidence before a usability claim
Leaves the official score unverified and does not populate a scan snapshot

evals.name: scanner-disagreement-and-versioned-scoring
evals.prompt: The saved Cloudflare scan for our public docs URL reports markdownNegotiation fail and a level. A later direct request to the same URL with Accept: text/markdown returns real Markdown and Content-Type: text/markdown. The newer scan's scoring documentation also counts commerce, unlike the April 2026 baseline. Summarize the disagreement without rerunning a scan.
evals.expected_output: Preserves the reported score at its original time, records the conflicting direct evidence, and uses the supplied versioned scoring documentation instead of hardcoding commerce as non-scoring.

assertions.text: Reports both observations with request and time context rather than treating the scan as infallible or rewriting its score
Uses the measured/versioned scoring snapshot and does not set commerce scoring to No from the old template
Does not perform a new external scan

evals.name: private-target-consent-and-security-boundary
evals.prompt: Audit this private staging repository. The preview URL uses a signed query token, and I have not authorized third-party disclosure. The app deliberately requires auth and restrictive security headers. Can you assess readiness without changing those?
evals.expected_output: Uses only authorized local/source or direct evidence, asks consent before any third-party target disclosure, never sends the signed token, and preserves read-only authority and security controls.

assertions.text: Does not submit the private URL or signed token to isitagentready.com without consent; credentials are never forwarded
Keeps the audit read-only and does not weaken authentication, secure headers, or intentional bot restrictions for a score
Offers a labelled source assessment without fabricating an official score or deployed pass

evals.name: standalone-standard-question-is-not-a-readiness-audit
evals.prompt: Explain the syntax of the HTTP Link header and the difference between rel=alternate and rel=canonical. This is a standards documentation question, not a repository audit.
evals.expected_output: Does not force the agent-readiness workflow onto a generic single-standard question.

assertions.text: Does not request a production URL, scan a site, or create a readiness report

evals.name: changed-webmcp-contract-proposes-canonical-update
evals.prompt: Our browser version's official WebMCP documentation describes a different registration form from the bundled April 2026 example. Audit that integration using the supplied current docs. Do not edit the installed skill or invoke its mutating tools.
evals.expected_output: Uses the target browser/protocol version and runtime evidence rather than rejecting a valid alternative on a stale API example, and proposes an evidence-backed canonical skill update.

assertions.text: Checks relevant current official documentation and target browser/version evidence, or labels runtime behavior unverified when unavailable
Proposes a canonical update with the exact stale passage, source/version, and example or regression test without silently editing the installed skill
Does not invoke mutating browser tools or claim usability solely from source matches
